$comment: FuzeFront's own policy, baselined from `--report` on 2026-10-05 (FuzeSDLC v1.23.0 gates). mode=ratchet: knownUnhandled only shrinks. The gate scripts and Harden Gate jobs arrive via governance-sync; this file sits here until then.
Policy for scripts/gate_event_envelope.py (gate-event-envelope) -- data-consistency-standard.md section 3 (envelope v2) and the TS<->Python registry-parity row of section 11.

registry.path / topicsPath / schemasDir locate this repo's TS event registry (the values below are FuzeFront's layout, the family convention). A repo that publishes no domain events at all replaces `registry`/`envelope`/`parity` with `notApplicable: { reason }` (>= 40 chars) -- a declared decision, printed on every run; a missing registry with no such declaration FAILS (absence is not permission).

envelope.v2Markers are regexes: a schema declaration matching ANY is on envelope v2; so is one naming every identifier in envelope.requiredFields (default eventId, aggregateType, aggregateId, aggregateVersion). The static check cannot see a schema built at run time -- widen the markers here rather than weakening the gate.

minTopics is the EXPECTED topic count and the non-vacuity floor: a registry that parses to fewer topics fails, so a moved/reshaped registry cannot pass by parsing to nothing. Set it to the current count; lower it only in a reviewed PR when topics are genuinely removed.

parity.pythonMirror is the Python registry file or package directory. If it does not exist the single finding is `parity:python-mirror-missing`: it is neither ignored nor green -- list it in knownUnhandled (inherited debt, shrink-only) or in exempt with a reason (a repo that will never have a Python side). Other parity items are `parity:<topic>` (in TS, absent from Python) and `parity-extra:<topic>` (the reverse).

knownUnhandled is a RATCHET, not an allowlist. An entry is only ever REMOVED. A new offender fails the gate immediately, and the gate also fails if a listed entry is now compliant (or gone) and has not been removed here in the same PR -- otherwise the list rots into a permanent exemption nobody revisits.

exempt[] is a declared, reasoned decision (reason >= 40 chars; standard section 13), not a way to make a red gate green. A name that matches nothing fails (stale exemption); a name in both exempt and knownUnhandled fails.

This file is SEEDED from FuzeSDLC and owned by THIS repo from then on: governance-sync does not overwrite it. Seed the baseline with `--report`, whose last block is a suggested knownUnhandled (replace, do not append).
knownUnhandled entries here are topic names (schema not yet on envelope v2) and `parity:*` items.
